title: Elmhurst Analytics - Extension & Sovereignty Check-in
summary: Quarterly renewal/check-in focused on contract extension, adding EU on-prem nodes for data residency, and modest capacity top-up. Main concerns: KMS integration, audit logs, latency SLOs and cost impact of dedicated vs hosted. Agreed to run a brief benchmark on their sample traffic and to share security pack + updated pricing amendment.
action_items: Marta Ruiz: Share sample inference trace and 24h traffic profile - due 2026-12-15
Priya Kapoor: Run 3-model benchmark on Elmhurst sample and deliver results + latency/cost tradeoffs - due 2026-12-20
Jordan Hayes: Draft contract amendment with 6-month extension and EU on-prem pilot clause - due 2026-12-18
Sofia Park: Provide list of compliance requirements and EFTS for KMS - due 2026-12-16
next_steps: Redwood to run benchmark on Elmhurst sample (Priya)
Share security documentation and KMS config guide (Jordan)
Schedule private pilot kickoff the week of 2027-01-04 if benchmark OK
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Marta (Elmhurst MLOps), Daniel (Elmhurst VP Eng), Sofia (Elmhurst Security), Leo (Elmhurst SRE)

[00:00] Jordan: Okay thanks everyone for joining, uh, happy Friday. I think we were scheduled for 50 minutes, we got about 3 items on the agenda — extension, EU onprem pilot and a small capacity uplift. Sound right?
[00:18] Marta: Yep that's right. Thanks Jordan. Quick note, we've got Daniel and Sofia here because on residency and compliance, they wanted to be involved.
[00:27] Daniel: hi all.
[00:29] Priya: hey, quick show of hands — anyone new to Redwoood console? I know the name always trips —
[00:35] Marta: i've used the dashboard, but not the private deploy flows.
[00:38] Liam: we'll run through the private pilot flow as part of the next steps.

[03:10] Jordan: High level — Elmhurst's current contract ends end of Q1 2027, you had asked about a short extension to keep continuity and to run an EU on-prem pilot for data residency. We're proposing a 6 month extension + a pilot that reserves two on-prem nodes in eu-west-1 footprint (customer-managed infra).
[03:38] Marta: Yes, that'll give our legal team breathing room. Main blocker for them is KMS/HSM approval and auditability of token usage.
[03:47] Sofia: Exactly. We need logs that show who called what model, and encrypted keys that we control. Also SOC2 evidence or equivalent.
[03:54] Jordan: Totally. Our security pack includes SOC2 docs, and we support KMS integration — we call it KMS passthrough in the docs, but sometimes the transcript from last time says "KMS past-through" — sorry the auto notes are messy. We'll attach the security pack after the call.

[06:02] Leo: On the on-prem side — how much of the runtime is customer-managed? We need to know if we'll be installing agents or running a full stack.
[06:12] Priya: For the pilot it's a lightweight private control plane plus your nodes running the runtime. You can choose the air-gapped installer or the containerized runtime. The runtime manages KV cache, batching, and the model serves. There is a small agent to manage health and metrics.
[06:27] Leo: Okay, and what about the KV cache — is that inprocess or remote? We've had issues in the past with KV cash miss rates (laughs, auto-transcribe again).
[06:38] Priya: it's an in-memory KV cache per host with optional shared redis for warm start. We'll share our recommended config for 8k token workloads.

[09:20] Daniel: On capacity — we're looking at +20% baseline tokens and a 2x burst capacity during business hours. Curious what impact that has on cost if we keep hosted vs move to dedicated pools.
[09:33] Jordan: Quick numbers — hosted is simplest but unit cost is higher; dedicated reserved pools bring predictable throughput and lower per-token cost but you commit month-to-month. For your volume, our calc suggests dedicated could save ~18% on per-token spend at your expected baseline, but burst capacity still incurs usage-based increments.
[09:53] Marta: Is there an option to do a hybrid — dedicated baseline + hosted overflow?
[09:58] Priya: Yes, smart routing supports tiered routing — primary to Dedicated (pinned region), fallback to Hosted, and also model variants if a quantized flavor is available. We'll include an example routing policy in the benchmark results.

[12:40] Sofia: On logs and audit — can we get token-level breakdowns, and per-request user-id? We need to tie calls back to internal user IDs for audit.
[12:50] Liam: Yes, token-level breakdown in Console and trace hooks are available, with per-route filters. For private deployments we can stream logs to your SIEM; we also support S3-like audit exports.

[15:10] Marta: Our legal asked about data retention — specifically whether Redwood stores any request payloads in hosted mode.
[15:18] Jordan: By default hosted request payloads are retained for 30 days for debugging, but enterprise contracts can change retention to 0 and enable verifiable zero-retention in the private mode. We'll show the exact clause in the amendment.

[18:05] Daniel: The team also wants a quick perf baseline — average p95 latency for our short-ctx prompts, and cost per 1k tokens for different quantization/ batching settings.
[18:14] Priya: We'll run a benchmark on your sample traffic. If you share a 72-hour trace (anonymized) with sequence length distribution, we'll run three variants: hosted baseline, dedicated pinned (no quant), and dedicated + 4-bit quantized model where we measure p50/p95 and cost delta.
[18:30] Marta: can we expect the quantized variant to change model quality? We have a few hallucination-sensitive flows.
[18:36] Priya: there can be small deltas for certain models; we'll include quality regressions on your prompt set — Redwood Optimize will flag regressions tied to prompt sets/evals.

[22:20] Jordan: timeline note — if benchmark results are acceptable, we can start on-prem pilot the week of Jan 4th. Pilot is 4 weeks: setup, dry-run, workload simulation, security sign-off. After successful pilot we roll a limited-production carve.
[22:36] Daniel: That aligns with internal roadmaps. Our chief wants production by March.

[25:00] Sofia: A few technical asks: 1) how does KMS key rotation look with your runtime? 2) Are audit logs tamper-evident? 3) Where do we host the HSM?
[25:10] Priya: 1) KMS integration supports customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiCorp Vault). Rotation is a handled handshake and we support key versioning in the runtime. 2) Logs can be sent to a write-once S3 bucket with object versioning and immutability; we recommend combining that with a hash-chain for tamper-evidence. 3) HSM can be customer-hosted or managed; for EU on-prem pilots many customers use a small HSM appliance in their colo and we support PKCS#11.

[29:50] Marta: Are there any SLA differences if we go dedicated vs hosted? We need 99.9% availability and p95 latency under 500ms for short queries.
[29:59] Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed throughput targets. Hosted SLA is softer, but most customers on hosted still meet <500ms p95 for short prompts. We'll map your exact traffic distribution to expected p95. If we can't meet p95 under committed baseline, we propose options: increase baseline, enable prefix caching, or route heavier flows to dedicated.

[33:15] Leo: Egress and billing — if we route overflow to hosted in a different region, how are egress costs handled?
[33:25] Jordan: We include egress in the usage invoices; if you route cross-region it will be visible as a separate line item. We can also do provider peering discounts in enterprise contracts.

[36:00] Daniel: About the contract amendment — can we get a 6-month auto-extension clause if pilot signoff is delayed? Our procurement team likes that buffer.
[36:10] Jordan: We can draft a clause for a 3-month automatic extension, but 6 months is possible if mutually agreed. I'll put a 6-month option in the draft and flag it for legal review.

[39:40] Priya: quick note on deployment ops — for the onprem pilot we'll provide a runbook, prometheus metrics exporter, and an observability dashboard template. That should make the SRE handoff much smoother.
[39:50] Leo: That helps, thanks.

[42:05] Marta: Anything else from Redwood?
[42:08] Jordan: We'll attach: 1) security pack (SOC2 reports, pen test summary), 2) onprem installer brief, 3) sample contract amendment, 4) benchmarking plan. Also will include a link to the shared spreadsheet for pricing scenarios. Link: https://drive.google.com/elmhurst/redwood-pricing-scenarios (note: placeholder).

[45:00] Sofia: We'll circulate the compliance checklist and let you know if anything else is required for KMS/HSM.

[47:22] Marta: Recap — Elmhurst to share sample traffic by Dec 15; Redwood to run benchmarks and send results by Dec 20; Jordan to send draft amendment by Dec 18; KMS/compliance items due Dec 16. Pilot kickoff week of Jan 4 pending OK.
[47:45] Jordan: Sounds good. Anything off the record? (laughs)
[47:50] Daniel: nope, all recorded.

[50:00] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with artifacts and next steps.
[50:05] Priya: thanks everyone.
[50:08] Marta: thanks.
